messages:
Jorge (Customer CTO): Morning — quick urgent heads-up. Our streaming clients with acme-health see event streams cut off without the closing event when a single data push is >~18KB. Happens from web and our mobile SDK. Billing shows duplicate charges because client reconnect resumes and counts twice. Rooted this at 10:02am UTC with a pcap attached.
Sam (Support): Thanks @Jorge. Do clients observe an HTTP error mid-stream or a 200 then silent end? Any client-side 401s? Also can you share a minimal repro payload and the pcap path.
Jorge (Customer CTO): Client gets 200, then the SSE stops (no final event). SDK logs show connection drop and immediate reconnect using resume token. No 401s in client logs. Pcap uploaded: /pcaps/acme-2004567890-edge.pcap
Sam (Support): Looping in runtime and SRE: @Priya @Maya — trace id trc_f1b2, req req_c3d4 in our logs. Priya, can runtime reproduce with that payload? Maya, check edge proxy resets and buffer metrics.
Priya (eng-runtime): On it. Need the exact raw SSE payload that hits ~18KB and any edge headers. Also, please confirm whether this org had any auth key rotation around the timeframe.
Jorge (Customer CTO): Payload and headers uploaded: /support-files/acme/payload_18k.json and headers_acme_10-02.txt. No client-side auth rotation observed but they do rotate server-side keys every hour.
Maya (eng-sre): Initial triage: edge shows a burst of downstream resets and some 499-like logs (client gone) at the same second as large event flows. Envoy proxy config on some older hosts uses proxy_buffer_size ~16384 (16KB). Observed metric sse.upstream_resets increased by 53 during the incident window. Attaching edge snippet:
```
[10:02:16] host=edge-12 upstream_reset reason: downstream_remote_reset bytes_sent=18432
[10:02:16] host=edge-12 downstream_response_code: 200
[10:02:16] host=edge-12 client_disconnect: true
```
Maya (eng-sre): That bytes_sent number is suspiciously exact — 18432 bytes.
Priya (eng-runtime): That lines up with buffer boundary behaviour. Two failure hypotheses: (A) proxy buffer overflow causing abrupt connection termination when a single SSE payload chunk exceeds buffer; (B) internal auth rotation causes upstream component to send 401 which triggers a stream teardown and resume. Need to correlate auth rotation timestamps.
Sam (Support): In API logs for req_c3d4 we have:
```
[10:02:11] req_c3d4 headers Authorization=Bearer tok_acme... x-forwarded-for=203.0.113.55
[10:02:16] upstream_reset: connection terminated, bytes_sent=18432
[10:02:16] resume_attempt token=rt_acme_77 success=true
[10:02:17] billing charge_id=chg_9001 duplicate_flag=true
```
Priya (eng-runtime): The timeline fits buffer cutoff at 18432, then client resume which generated a second billable session. We need to prevent double-billing on resume or ensure stream integrity so resume isn't counted as a new charge before verifying finalization.
Maya (eng-sre): Confirmed an auth key rotation event landed at 10:02:15 for org acme-health on internal key-rotate service. However, no 401 surfaced in client logs. It's possible an internal component performed a check and returned 401 to the upstream pool, causing a reset concurrently with the buffer cutoff — a race.
Jorge (Customer CTO): Repro commands we used locally (worked ~90% reproducible):
```
# raw SSE using curl
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams?model=orca" -o /tmp/stream.out
# python SSE test
python3 examples/sse_tester.py --token $TOKEN --url https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams --event-file payload_18k.json
```
Sam (Support): Short-term mitigation for you: can you enable event chunking in the client and split events to <8KB? Does that prevent truncation and duplicate billing?
Jorge (Customer CTO): We tried chunking to 8KB and first run looked clean — stream finished with final event and billing duplicates stopped. We'll keep that while you provide a fix.
Priya (eng-runtime): Long-term options: (1) runtime can detect large single SSE events and automatically split into smaller sub-events to avoid proxy buffer triggers; (2) infra can increase proxy buffer (envoy proxy_buffer_size) and enable chunked transfer semantics for SSE path; (3) billing dedupe by resume_token to avoid double-charging overlapping sessions. I'll open a PR for the runtime guard to split >12KB events.
Maya (eng-sre): I'll file an infra ticket to change proxy buffers on the older fleet and run a canary. Also adding an SLO alert: sse.upstream_resets > 5 in 5m triggers pager. Ticket INF-3321 created and canary scheduled.
Priya (eng-runtime): Repro plan for devs:
1) Run a local envoy instance with proxy_buffer_size set to 16k to reproduce the truncation.
2) Stream the 18,432-byte payload and observe downstream reset and runtime behavior.
Local test commands:
```
docker run --rm -p 10000:10000 envoyproxy/envoy:v1.30 -c /etc/envoy/local_sse_test.yaml
python3 tests/send_sse_event.py --size 18432 --token tok_test --url http://localhost:10000/v1/streams
```
Priya (eng-runtime): I'll run that and patch the runtime to split events >12k into multiple SSE data: frames. Adding unit test and integration test against envoy to ensure no upstream_reset.
Sam (Support): Observability actions for now:
- Attach edge logs and the pcap (we have both from Jorge).
- Add a histogram metric sse.event_size.bytes and a counter sse.resume_token_duplicates to detect billing duplications.
- Log resume_token with request id on resume attempts for dedupe insight.
Maya (eng-sre): Implementing sse.event_size.hist and an alert rule. Also will add automated nightly check: if any upstream_reset spike occurs that correlates with bytes_sent ~= 16384 +/- 256 bytes, create a paging incident for infra.
Sam (Support): @Jorge — we're treating this as high priority. Short term: keep client chunking. Eng will provide patch; infra will roll buffer fix via canary. We'll also follow up on billing dedupe.
deploy-bot: INF-3321 created and assigned to infra-team: https://redwood.example/infrastructure/INF-3321
Jorge (Customer CTO): Confirmed after client chunking: no truncation and no duplicate charges on two separate tests. Thanks. We'll leave work to your teams for a permanent fix.
Priya (eng-runtime): Will open runtime PR with guard to split >12KB SSE payloads and a unit test. Target is next patch release. Also adding an integration test that runs envoy in CI to assert no upstream_reset.
Maya (eng-sre): Rolling canary for proxy_buffer_size bump and adding the alert. Also adding logging for resume_token and billing dedupe flags.
Sam (Support): Next steps recap:
- Customer: continue using chunking for now and share any additional repros.
- Eng-runtime: PR for automatic split + tests.
- Infra: INF-3321, canary for buffer increase.
- Billing: add resume_token dedupe or grace window to avoid double-charge on immediate resume.
Sam (Support): Closing this thread for now and reassigning to eng-runtime + infra for follow-ups. Will update acme-health when changes land. :thumbsup:
